handling.actualEgressStatement: Approved local public-repository metadata, selected source/document content and derived findings were processed in the active OpenAI Codex session. Assessment collection used no network provider, registry, scanner or remote GitHub/CI query. The user separately authorized commits and pushes of reviewed assessment artifacts to the existing origin remote.
redactions: No raw source excerpts, credential values, private overlays or author identities are included.
Evidence uses portable repository-relative paths; aggregate counts and team roles replace personal activity.

permissionsGaps.impact: The report is partial; missing evidence is not a pass and no numeric maturity score or delivery authorization is inferred.
permissionsGaps.summary: This static STRIDE/misuse-case review did not execute attacks, fetch external sources, inspect provider controls or assess every guide's lab safety. Threat likelihood and residual exploitability remain unmeasured.
Service region, retention/deletion and approval expiry are not supplied by local repository evidence.
permissionsGaps.impact: Owner governance details remain unknown; assessment findings await user review.

findings.title: URL-opening paths do not enforce permitted schemes at the call boundary
findings.description: Bandit reported three B310 observations in the official-study-guide monitor. The general fetch path and two Oracle guest-session requests call urllib URL opening without an explicit scheme check at those call sites. The inputs are normally official catalog URLs, but a changed or malformed catalog value can reach the fetch boundary, so the scanner cannot establish that file or custom schemes are rejected.

remediation.summary: Validate each outbound URL against the intended HTTPS scheme and approved host policy immediately before opening it.
steps: Define the permitted scheme and host rules for generic official-source retrieval and the Oracle guest-session flow.
Reject non-HTTPS URLs and unexpected hosts before constructing or opening a request.
Add regression cases for file, custom, malformed, redirect, and unexpected-host inputs.
Rerun Bandit and the existing monitor tests after a separately approved implementation change.

findings.title: A guide-only change does not invalidate the default AI-audit completion key
findings.description: completed_current_audits and select_batch key completed work by exam code, blueprint snapshot hash and rubric version. The schema does not bind the result to guide content. Consequently a changed explanation or lab can remain excluded from default selection while its blueprint is unchanged. This is inferred from the key and selection condition; no runtime re-audit was executed.

remediation.summary: Bind future audit results and default selection to the reviewed guide revision or content digest.
steps: Specify immutable evidence for the guide, blueprint and rubric reviewed together.
Preserve older audits as historical records rather than inventing guide digests for them.
Add a case where only guide content changes and verify that the guide becomes eligible for re-audit.

findings.title: Independent content-assurance coverage trails the published library
findings.description: The repository contains 222 guides, while the current independent AI-audit ledger covers 39 guides and the freshness ledger covers 33. Ten AI-audit findings remain open, 61 source candidates remain queued, and no guide is marked community-reviewed. Source-validation records and automated checks cover important structural concerns, but they are not substitutes for the independent semantic and freshness layers defined by this repository.

remediation.summary: Continue risk-ranked independent audit and freshness batches, resolve the ten open findings, and establish an explicit human-review sampling target before treating library-wide quality as assured.
steps: Prioritize the 183 guides without an AI-audit result and the 189 guides without a freshness result using lifecycle volatility, exam criticality, and change history.
Resolve or explicitly disposition the ten currently open AI-audit findings before expanding lower-risk coverage.
Define a review cadence and a bounded human community-review sample with recorded acceptance criteria.
Verify that the ledgers reconcile to the 222-guide inventory and publish coverage counts without converting them into permanent quality labels.

findings.title: CI validation is duplicated and dependency-update coverage is partial
findings.description: The validation and Pages workflows repeat the same unit, repository, strict-build, and site-validation sequence. Dependabot is configured only for GitHub Actions even though the site has three pinned Python dependencies, and workflow actions use mutable major-version references. These local definitions create maintenance drift and supply-chain review work; remote enforcement and run health could not be assessed.

remediation.summary: Centralize the shared validation sequence, add governed Python dependency updates, and adopt a documented action-reference policy.
steps: Extract the common validation sequence into one reusable workflow or composite local action used by validation and deployment.
Add a pip Dependabot entry for requirements-site.txt with a review cadence appropriate for the site toolchain.
Decide and document whether third-party action references must be pinned to full commit SHAs, with an update mechanism that keeps them current.
Verify both pull-request validation and Pages deployment consume the same validation definition.
